events.categories: Indepth / Free A&C Events / Other / West
events.description:
A zine workshop in the Chillzone at VEEM, with a guest collective invited by Hothead. A day of researching, gathering and making, moving between music, quotes, images, words, references and random finds.From deep dives to things found by accident, from personal archives to things that should belong to everyone. The workshop explores the art of self-publishing and how collecting different things can turn into something new. Participants will work towards their own publication, made from the references, ideas and materials gathered along the way.

events.title: GINGA: VIRA Exhibition
events.subtitle: Free Public Exhibition
events.categories: Exhibitions / Free A&C Events / Funk / Baile Funk / East
events.description:
"Vira", in Portuguese, means to turn or transform something — a situation, a scenario — in a positive way. VIRA becomes the cultural link between Brazil and the Netherlands, pulsing with music, art, nightlife, and the vibrant energy of both countries.

During ADE Week, Studio/K will be transformed into a free public exhibition space where photography, film, and digital storytelling come together. A photography exhibition featuring images from São Paulo and Amsterdam highlights the connections between the two cities.

The program concludes with an indepth session on the 24th of October featuring members of Encosta and ONDA Collective, followed by "Beats & Bites," an informal networking event that brings together artists, musicians, creatives, visitors, and professionals from the Dutch and Brazilian creative sectors.

The exhibition is free to visit. Open Wed-Sat 16:00-22:00.

events.subtitle: A Brazilian musical drama
events.categories: Indepth / Film & Documentaries / Funk / Baile Funk / East
events.description:
In addition to the open deck session and exhibition, the film Funk (2026) will be screened on ADE Wednesday. Directed by Aly Muritiba, the film follows Sabrina, a young funk artist from the favelas of Rio de Janeiro, as she navigates the competitive baile funk scene. Set against a backdrop of heavy beats, bold performances, and the energy of the dance floor, the film explores themes of ambition, class, and the tension between commercial success and staying true to your roots.The screening will be followed by a post-film discussion with a guest speaker (TBC), fitting seamlessly within Encosta and ONDA Collective’s ADE programme. Like the rest of Studio/K’s ADE programme, Funk highlights baile funk not only as a music genre but as a cultural force that brings together community, creativity, and self-expression, connecting Brazil’s underground scene with contemporary club culture.

events.description: This is not a regular concert.Come trip on the avant-garde sound world of Sofia Gubaidulina - the composer the Soviets tried to ban for being too radical - and the trance-ambient music of Soheil Shayesteh, live in one of Amsterdam's most beautiful hidden gems: the Uilenburgersjoel.Lay down. Let the sound move through the space and through you. There's no stage to face, no seat you're expected to sit still in - just a shifting, physical body of sound built to take you somewhere else, inside a 17th-century synagogue most of Amsterdam has never set foot in.The music itself moves in two directions at once. Gubaidulina's world is raw, confrontational, rooted in the physical - it pulls you down into the earth. events.title: Rethinking Dance in Nightlife
events.subtitle: presented by The Better Move
events.categories: Indepth / Dance & Theatre / Free A&C Events / House / West
events.description:
Lately we've observed fewer dancers on the dancefloor, fewer dancers hired or planned as part of an event's programming, and audiences standing facing the DJ with their phones out. What happened to dancing all night long, connecting to the music and to each other? Have we lost the essence of clubbing?

This indepth session is organized in the context of The Better Move, a project supported by VibeLab. Its goal is to increase the employment of dance professionals in the nighttime economy, and integrate more movement-based, health-enhancing, and culturally rooted experiences into club programming.

This event is donation-based. Would you like to support our work? You can donate via the QR code on the day of the event.

events.title: Listening Session & Bites with Disco Arabesquo
events.subtitle: A journey into the world of Egyptian film music
events.categories: Live Performances / Exhibitions / Live / Other / New West / New Arts & Culture Venues
events.description:
What does a film sound like if you take away the visuals? During this special ADE listening session, DJ Disco Arabesquo dives into his collection of vinyl and cassettes, taking you into the world of Egyptian film music from the 70s, 80s, and 90s.‍Expect unique soundtracks, hidden gems, and music you might recognize without knowing where you’ve heard it before. With this listening session, Disco Arabesquo shares his love for the music, the films, and the culture in which these sounds continue to live on outside the cinema.‍In addition, Qibli Bahri will provide delicious Egyptian snacks, so you can dive into ADE with a well-filled stomach. You can also explore the exhibition Dreams of Films - Films of Dreams. Please note: we are keeping this event small and intimate, so don't wait too long to buy your tickets.

The exhibition Dreams of Films - Films of Dreams is part of ADE Arts & Culture.

15 dancers explore the state of nightlife, post-clubbing.

“Wonderful and devastating performance (…) Definitely the most impressive group work I saw in years.” Fransien van der Putt, dramaturg, theatre critic and author.

Elisa Zuppini choreographs a system in which human perception converges with other-than-human agencies. Fifteen dancers form a pulsing structure, extending toward and withdrawing from the audience’s perceptual field. Like chthonic waves, they generate a hybrid circuit of sensation.Within the insomniac framework of post-clubbing, the dancers explore the effects and aftereffects of hedonistic nightlife. events.categories: Dance & Theatre / Other / Centre / Club Culture
events.description:
It’s sexy, thrilling and thought-provoking!

Striptopia is a captivating two-hour show that challenges stigma and celebrates the art forms of pole dance, drag, stripping and performance. This reimagined strip club is built on the values of honesty, safety, inclusivity and joy.Striptopia brings you face to face with outspoken performers in a fully interactive experience, where tipping via the Striptopia App, cheering and making contact are encouraged. Here, strip-club culture becomes something to celebrate, reflect on and reappraise.

About Striptopia:This isn’t a strip club relocated; it’s strip culture turned inside out. Built on consent, inclusivity and performer autonomy, Striptopia is a space where respect and celebration go hand in hand. Performers own their stage and boundaries, while guests are invited to explore and let go responsibly.

The workshop is designed for young adults aged 18 to 30. Expect a creative evening set in the inspiring surroundings of the Rijksmuseum. events.title: Sonic Journey: The History of Electronic Dance Music
events.subtitle: A musical journey through time
events.categories: Live Performances / House / Techno / Other / South / Club Culture / Deep Listening & Spatial Sound
events.description:
On ADE Wednesday - whether lying down or sitting up - embark on a musical journey through time. A musical story that begins in Jamaica, with music by artists such as Donna Summer, Grandmaster Flash, and Kraftwerk, and - via Frankie Knuckles and Juan Atkins - passes through Chicago and Detroit before finally ending in Europe, and thus also in Amsterdam. The evening will feature hosts and DJs Nathan Kofi and Derk Louwes. The event will be conducted in English.For this unique event, only the seats next to the stage and a limited number of spots to lie down on the stage itself will be sold. This means the stage is rotated 180 degrees compared to the normal setup at The Concertgebouw's Main Hall.

Please bring your own mat if you wish to lie down.

Art Bar SEXYLAND is a café you visit on Wednesdays when you’re stuck in your ideas, a place to talk about art or show your work to a renowned artist or curator from the field, who happens to be your bartender for the night.

It offers emerging and established artists an informal way to ask questions without the formality of a traditional Q&A, because the person you’re talking to is simply standing behind the bar. The credo is bad bartenders, great ideas, so awkwardness is something we all share. events.description: One monumental art installation. Two weeks on view. Four extraordinary concerts. Celebrate ADE’s 30th anniversary with EINDER by Boris Acket.On 21 October, monumental music, art and architecture come together to celebrate 30 years of ADE.The Concertgebouworkest will perform Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony with 70 musicians inside Amsterdam’s monumental Centrale Markthal. Enjoy this true classic from 1808 conducted by Riccardo Minasi, beneath the largest-ever version of Boris Acket’s EINDER.The rhythmic motif of Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony is repeated constantly, taking on ever-changing forms, and in this way Beethoven builds his symphony layer by layer. While EINDER will shift and reshape above the orchestra creating a dance that is never the same twice.Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony was revolutionary 200 years ago, and it still is today. This energetic music never ceases to surprise.About EINDERE

15 dancers explore the state of nightlife, post-clubbing.

“Wonderful and devastating performance (…) Definitely the most impressive group work I saw in years.” Fransien van der Putt, dramaturg, theatre critic and authorElisa Zuppini choreographs a system in which human perception converges with other-than-human agencies. events.description:

Shaped by Wes Broersen’s scenography, the performance draws the audience into a charged atmosphere where minimalism, emotion, and visual space resonate as one. From the work’s poised stillness emerges a hypnotic intensity, revealing the subtle power of Glass’ distinctive musical language.

'Glass' repetition creates a sense of ceremonial momentum'

events.description: Every person who walks into Charged becomes exactly that. A cloud of light gathers around you, pulled in by your presence, and moves when you move. Some people you meet in it carry the same charge as you, and so push each other's energy away. Others carry the opposite, and your clouds fold into each other before either of you has decided to merge. As magnetic poles repel, opposites attract.The work is about how we change each other's environment simply by being in it, positively or negatively, whether we mean to or not. Charging and discharging as a way of interacting between persons. The more people step in, the more chaotic it becomes. Heliotrope is a kinetic installation inspired by the natural phenomenon in which plants orient their leaves and blossoms toward the sun. The work takes this principle as both a biological reference and a metaphor, exploring processes of energy reception, tropistic behaviour, the atomic movements inherent to living matter, and the pulsating rhythms embedded within the natural world. This idea is translated into a mirrored installation. The mechanically engineered installation moves its blades, diffusing light beams, and reflecting its surroundings in a chaotic and refracted image. events.title: Melting Image
events.subtitle: The longer you look, the more it changes.
events.categories: Exhibitions / Free A&C Events / Other / Centre
events.description:
Melting Image is a quiet resistance to how we consume images today — against the passive, one-dimensional scroll of the digital screen, it asks for presence instead of speed. Here, looking takes time, and the image only reveals itself to those willing to give it.An image is silkscreened onto layers of transparent material, then heat-formed until it lifts off the flat surface and takes on an organic, sculptural shape. Displayed in the gallery window, it turns the glass into a screen between street and space. Lit from behind by a slowly shifting projection, each layer catches the colour differently: parts of the image surface, others fade, never quite settling into one form. The longer you look, the more it keeps changing.Romina Koopman is a visual artist working at the edge of the tangible and the virtual, questioning how the digital image reshapes our perception of reality.

Visitors can interact with the sleeping babies in real time by inputting sound through a microphone, connecting with them via the ChatGPT system. events.title: Deep Seeing Currents
events.subtitle: An evocative deep-sea experience by Olafur Eliasson
events.categories: Exhibitions / Audiovisual & Immersive Arts / Beyond the Dancefloor / Other / Centre / New Arts & Culture Venues / Deep Listening & Spatial Sound
events.description:
As you approach Deep Seeing Currents by Olafur Eliasson, you are slowly enveloped by darkness and the sounds of life underwater. Layers of oceanic cacophony – whale songs, rumbling of hydrothermal vents, and human-made noises, among others – surround you, while the vibrations can be felt throughout your entire body, emulating the experience of pressure in the deep sea. Above and around you, lights flash and seem to descend like the hypnotic circulation of marine snow, the organic and inorganic particles essential to life in the deep sea.The immersive sound of Deep seeing currents is brought to life by 4DSOUND. The exhibition is located inside the ARTIS Aquarium and can be visited with a valid ARTIS Park ticket. Tickets are available through the ARTIS website.

events.description:
Pantheon Amsterdam brings together contemporary art, heritage and spirituality in a unique exhibition at Museum Ons’ Lieve Heer op Solder. Eight artists are creating new altarpieces and celebrations centred on stories of faith, identity, exclusion and recognition. Pantheon Amsterdam demonstrates that these subjects are not merely historical phenomena, but contemporary themes that continue to give meaning to the lives of many people.

One of these art installations is ‘Opacity’ by Sammie Tjon Sien Foek, also known as DJ Slimfit. During ADE, Slimfit will give three intimate performances in the museum’s clandestine church. By integrating and remixing classical music elements with live electronic composition influenced by ancestral rhythms, they reinterpret supposedly opposing liturgical ideologies. More information about the performances at this page.

events.categories: Exhibitions / Beyond the Dancefloor / Other / Centre
events.description:
Initiated by artist Lawil Karama in conversation with historian Megan Hoetger, The Nature of Remembering is a group exhibition featuring multimedia research projects that move between interrogation of normative memory politics and co-experimentation with environmental and more-than-human bodies.The exhibition title carries in it two meanings: on the one hand, nature is evoked, drawing focus to actants, actors, and animacies beyond and beside the human, who witness, participate in, index, recollect, foretell, and haunt historical time. On the other hand, the idiomatic expression "the nature of" is taken up as a provocation, pushing against pervasive ideological and violently enforced notions of remembering and of commemorating.

events.description: 99 years ago, Layla was filmed; the first Egyptian feature film. This marked the beginning of a film culture that became one of the shared languages ​​of the Arab world for decades.This exhibition, Dreams of Films – Films of Dreams, by Van Eesteren Museum and Moataz Rageb, brings back the visual world of cinema from that era. Here, you will discover original cinema posters, hand-painted billboards, and illustrated posters created by illustrators, calligraphers, and printers who are rarely known by name.In addition to images, sound and music also take center stage. Film music has always been inextricably linked to Egyptian cinema, and famous compositions were revived through another medium: on cassette tapes. Rembrandt’s De Nachtwacht became the starting point for a new artistic work by Jeff Mills, created and filmed inside the Rijksmuseum.Mills studied Rembrandt’s masterpiece and responded to it through his own art, bringing together electronic music, dance and visual art. The resulting film has never been publicly shown.As part of ADE’s 30th anniversary, the film will be unveiled to the public for the very first time — returning to the very space in which it was conceived.From Thursday 22 to Sunday 25 October, the 50-minute film will be presented three times a day in the Rijksmuseum auditorium.Timeslots will be at 12PM, 2PM and 4PM.Admission is free and includes entry to the Rijksmuseum, courtesy of KPN as connectivity partner.Sign up before October 11, 23.59 to receive access by email to the tick

events.title: Sound, Technology and Consciousness by Museum of Consciousness
events.subtitle: Perspectives from the Museum of Consciousness
events.categories: Indepth / Ambient & Listening / Other / Centre / Deep Listening & Spatial Sound
events.description:
The session opens with sound transmissions from the Museum of Consciousness, followed by a talk by Carl Hayden Smith exploring how sound can transform perception, attention and our experience of reality. How does sound shape consciousness, and how might emerging technologies extend our capacity to listen, feel and perceive? Drawing on immersive artistic practice, psychoacoustics and archaeoacoustics, Smith explores the relationship between sound, embodiment, memory and altered states of consciousness.Moving between ancient acoustic traditions, contemporary technologies and scientific enquiry, the session examines the therapeutic potential of sound and asks a fundamental question: Can extraordinary listening experiences produce lasting changes in how we perceive, feel and act?

Futures of Listening comes to Amsterdam Dance Event 2026 with Currents, a four-day programme of experiments and performances in spatial sound at Loods6, from 22 to 25 October. events.title: Public Try Out: White Space + Popup by ICK-Next
events.subtitle: presented by Harmonic Dissonance
events.categories: Exhibitions / Audiovisual & Immersive Arts / Other / New West / New Arts & Culture Venues
events.description:
A monochromatic light instrument played through collective presence.White Space is an immersive installation that transforms negative space into a place where strangers connect.

At its heart, a monolith of intense blue and white light spins on its axis, casting compositions of monochromatic light and generative music that shift and dance among the audience. Responding to pose and position, the sculpture becomes an instrument, played by everyone present at once.

Only by coordinating their positions and synchronising their poses can visitors reach the climax of the installation: illuminating the emptiness that separates them and transforming the negative space into White Space.

events.title: Hoketus 50!
events.subtitle: A work that forever changed the landscape of new music
events.categories: Live Performances / Beyond the Dancefloor / Contemporary / Live / East
events.description:
Uncompromising in form and driven by a rhythmic energy that defies all convention – that is Hoketus, the legendary composition by Louis Andriessen.Fifty years ago, Andriessen wrote this still-striking piece that reshaped the face of contemporary music. Hoketus became a cornerstone of the Dutch musical movement known as the Haagse School (The Hague School) and an enduring source of inspiration far beyond the Netherlands. Many composers have drawn from Andriessen’s propulsive rhythms, minimalist precision, and raw sonic world.For this anniversary celebration, Michael Gordon, co-founder of the legendary Bang on a Can collective, writes a mirror composition: a new work that confronts Hoketushead-on. Not a homage, but a next step in the path Andriessen set out – music that doesn’t yield, but clashes, moves, and breaks.

events.categories: Nighttime events / All night long / House
events.description:
Thuishaven is not a club, or a warehouse. It’s a unique experience. Located on the Western outskirts of Amsterdam, the site is surrounded by heavy industry, massive oil tankers and scrap metal yards. Thuishaven has several stages, bars, surreal decoration pieces and curiosities. Incorporating materials purchased or found at neighboring scrap yards, the site radiates a raw and industrial atmosphere. During the winter set-up (October - April), all stages are housed indoor, in heated tents and a newly crafted hangar. The summer set-up (May - September) hosts a mesmerizing open air stage plus the option to use both tent and hangar for a raveyer vibe. With a track record of 200 festivals and counting, the site is ever evolving. Every new visit brings to light new details and new surprises—making it one of Amsterdam’s most extraordinary venues.

events.description: Every person who walks into Charged becomes exactly that. A cloud of light gathers around you, pulled in by your presence, and moves when you move. Some people you meet in it carry the same charge as you, and so push each other's energy away. Others carry the opposite, and your clouds fold into each other before either of you has decided to merge. As magnetic poles repel, opposites attract.The work is about how we change each other's environment simply by being in it, positively or negatively, whether we mean to or not. Charging and discharging as a way of interacting between persons. The more people step in, the more chaotic it becomes. events.title: Melting Image
events.subtitle: The longer you look, the more it changes.
events.categories: Exhibitions / Free A&C Events / Other / Centre
events.description:
Melting Image is a quiet resistance to how we consume images today — against the passive, one-dimensional scroll of the digital screen, it asks for presence instead of speed. Here, looking takes time, and the image only reveals itself to those willing to give it.An image is silkscreened onto layers of transparent material, then heat-formed until it lifts off the flat surface and takes on an organic, sculptural shape. Displayed in the gallery window, it turns the glass into a screen between street and space. Lit from behind by a slowly shifting projection, each layer catches the colour differently: parts of the image surface, others fade, never quite settling into one form. The longer you look, the more it keeps changing.Romina Koopman is a visual artist working at the edge of the tangible and the virtual, questioning how the digital image reshapes our perception of reality.

events.title: Deep Seeing Currents
events.subtitle: An evocative deep-sea experience by Olafur Eliasson
events.categories: Exhibitions / Audiovisual & Immersive Arts / Beyond the Dancefloor / Other / Centre / New Arts & Culture Venues / Deep Listening & Spatial Sound
events.description:
As you approach Deep Seeing Currents by Olafur Eliasson, you are slowly enveloped by darkness and the sounds of life underwater. Layers of oceanic cacophony – whale songs, rumbling of hydrothermal vents, and human-made noises, among others – surround you, while the vibrations can be felt throughout your entire body, emulating the experience of pressure in the deep sea. Above and around you, lights flash and seem to descend like the hypnotic circulation of marine snow, the organic and inorganic particles essential to life in the deep sea.The immersive sound of Deep seeing currents is brought to life by 4DSOUND. The exhibition is located inside the ARTIS Aquarium and can be visited with a valid ARTIS Park ticket. Tickets are available through the ARTIS website.

Pantheon Amsterdam brings together contemporary art, heritage and spirituality in a unique exhibition at Museum Ons’ Lieve Heer op Solder. Eight artists are creating new altarpieces and celebrations centred on stories of faith, identity, exclusion and recognition. Pantheon Amsterdam demonstrates that these subjects are not merely historical phenomena, but contemporary themes that continue to give meaning to the lives of many people.

One of these art installations is ‘Opacity’ by Sammie Tjon Sien Foek, also known as DJ Slimfit. During ADE, Slimfit will give three intimate performances in the museum’s clandestine church. By integrating and remixing classical music elements with live electronic composition influenced by ancestral rhythms, they reinterpret supposedly opposing liturgical ideologies. More information about the performances at this page.

events.title: The Nature of Remembering
events.subtitle: Group exhibition initiated by Lawil Karama, in conversation with Megan Hoetger
events.categories: Exhibitions / Beyond the Dancefloor / Other / Centre
events.description:
Initiated by artist Lawil Karama in conversation with historian Megan Hoetger, The Nature of Remembering is a group exhibition featuring multimedia research projects that move between interrogation of normative memory politics and co-experimentation with environmental and more-than-human bodies.The exhibition title carries in it two meanings: on the one hand, nature is evoked, drawing focus to actants, actors, and animacies beyond and beside the human, who witness, participate in, index, recollect, foretell, and haunt historical time. On the other hand, the idiomatic expression "the nature of" is taken up as a provocation, pushing against pervasive ideological and violently enforced notions of remembering and of commemorating.

events.title: Dreams of Films – Films of Dreams
events.subtitle: An exhibition by Disco Arabesquo about the visual world of Egyptian cinema
events.categories: Exhibitions / Beyond the Dancefloor / Other / New West / New Arts & Culture Venues
events.description: 99 years ago, Layla was filmed; the first Egyptian feature film. This marked the beginning of a film culture that became one of the shared languages ​​of the Arab world for decades.This exhibition, Dreams of Films – Films of Dreams, by Van Eesteren Museum and Moataz Rageb, brings back the visual world of cinema from that era. Here, you will discover original cinema posters, hand-painted billboards, and illustrated posters created by illustrators, calligraphers, and printers who are rarely known by name.In addition to images, sound and music also take center stage. Film music has always been inextricably linked to Egyptian cinema, and famous compositions were revived through another medium: on cassette tapes. Rembrandt’s De Nachtwacht became the starting point for a new artistic work by Jeff Mills, created and filmed inside the Rijksmuseum.Mills studied Rembrandt’s masterpiece and responded to it through his own art, bringing together electronic music, dance and visual art. events.description: Rehearsal of the Victory Day Gig is developed from online meetings that helped _mediaklub stay together during lockdown and, later, during Russia’s war against Ukraine. When Max Robotov joined the Ukrainian Army, while others were separated by cities, countries, and time zones, this format became a way to remain close and continue working. Delays, glitches, and interruptions that once made collective music-making almost impossible became the structure of the work. The performance is built around Max’s voice from the front line, his commands, and the attempt to play together through unstable connection and distance. The _mediaklub group is based on the idea of an open visual and sound environment, the creation of which, at any stage, can be joined by members of the Ukrainian community of new media – Photinus. DISCO changed nightlife forever. But how did it all begin? What did Amsterdam sound like when the first disco records drifted in from New York? Who was there at the forefront when everything was still new, raw and exciting? events.description: On the second evening of the ADE Arts & Culture programme, ROZENSTRAAT presents Sidario (2025-26) by Peruvian artist Wynnie Mynerva. Blood and a white shroud are the central materials of Mynerva’s performance, which is inspired by Loco afán: Crónicas de sidario (1996) by Chilean writer and performer Pedro Lemebel. In this work, Lemebel describes the lives and mortality of gay and trans people during the AIDS crisis.In Sidario, HIV is addressed not only as a medical condition, but also as a social and political issue. Mynerva brings together HIV, sex work, gender, racialisation and death with the exclusion and neglect experienced by certain bodies. events.title: Futures of Listening presents: Currents | Configuration II
events.subtitle: An experimental night on the new Ambrio Spatial DJ mixer
events.categories: Live Performances / Electro & Wave / Alternative Electronic / Live / East / New Arts & Culture Venues / Deep Listening & Spatial Sound
events.description:
Futures of Listening comes to Amsterdam Dance Event 2026 with Currents, a four-day programme of experiments and performances in spatial sound at Loods6, from 22 to 25 October. Across three evenings of live and DJ sets, a day of workshops and demos, and a closing spatial sound meetup, artists work with changing sound system configurations to shape a different listening experience each night.The programme takes place in the concrete Bagagehall of Loods6, a former passenger and freight terminal on the edge of the IJ. Speakers small and large are placed along the length of the hall, and sound moves between them across heights and distances. Currents is an experiment in what sound in space can mean: visitors can sit, lie down and walk through the space while performances take place at various points along the corridor.

events.title: Archiving the Night: Expo Opening by State-OFFF & MRLYN
events.subtitle: A program on collecting Amsterdam's club and night culture
events.categories: Exhibitions / Free A&C Events / Other / West / Club Culture / New Arts & Culture Venues
events.description: An evening program organized in collaboration with the ADE Arts & Culture program and Podiumkunst.net, presented as part of the Amsterdam Museum's 100th anniversary: a special program on collecting club culture.For decades, Amsterdam's club culture has been a breeding ground for art, music, and social movements. From the legendary venues of the 1980s to today's nightlife scene, these are stories that have shaped the city. Yet this heritage is largely absent from official archives and collections. How do we ensure that the history of Amsterdam's nightlife is preserved, and for whom?Especially for ADE, we present two art installations that each form an archive for night and club culture in their own way. On October 23rd, a special opening program kicks things off, in which we talk with makers MRLYN and State OFFF about their perspective on the night and how it translates into their artwork

events.description: With raw, hypnotic beats, exhilarating chants and heavy basses, Arsenal Mikebe has steadily been infiltrating the international avant-garde. events.description: For the first time, ERRATIC WEATHER is presented in an immersive full-dome environment. Scientific data—including geolocation, atmospheric pressure, temperature and wind speed—forms the foundation for a unique composition of sound and visuals. No two performances are ever the same. Thuishaven is not a club, or a warehouse. It’s a unique experience. Located on the Western outskirts of Amsterdam, the site is surrounded by heavy industry, massive oil tankers and scrap metal yards. Thuishaven has several stages, bars, surreal decoration pieces and curiosities. Incorporating materials purchased or found at neighboring scrap yards, the site radiates a raw and industrial atmosphere. During the winter set-up (October - April), all stages are housed indoor, in heated tents and a newly crafted hangar. The summer set-up (May - September) hosts a mesmerizing open air stage plus the option to use both tent and hangar for a raveyer vibe. events.description:
Part of ADE Arts & Culture, co-curated with Amsterdam Light Festival.

Amsterdam-based Touki Delphine is a boundary-pushing collective of musicians, performers, and visual artists. They are making waves both nationally and internationally with monumental light and sound installations, built from recycled materials: taillights in FIREBIRD, turn signal relays in RELAY, wiring in TRANSMISSION, windshield washer fluid reservoirs and their pump motors in DRIFTING. Their latest work, SUPERDRUM, is constructed from second-hand drums, wooden branches, and car door lock mechanisms.Through their work, they create musical poetic encounters between humans and machines. Inspired by natural systems, the climate crisis and the idea of nature as a living whole, they imagine a future in which people, nature and technology collaborate rather than compete, and where waste can be transformed into something

events.title: Charged by Jaco Schilp
events.subtitle: Free light installation at ADE Lab Village
events.categories: Audiovisual & Immersive Arts / Free A&C Events / Other / West
events.description: Every person who walks into Charged becomes exactly that. A cloud of light gathers around you, pulled in by your presence, and moves when you move. Some people you meet in it carry the same charge as you, and so push each other's energy away. Others carry the opposite, and your clouds fold into each other before either of you has decided to merge. As magnetic poles repel, opposites attract.The work is about how we change each other's environment simply by being in it, positively or negatively, whether we mean to or not. Charging and discharging as a way of interacting between persons. The more people step in, the more chaotic it becomes. With only a few, it settles into something calm and connected.The visuals in Charged were built with TouchDesigner, while its eye uses an open-source AI vision model called YOLO, which has become the standard way for a machine to find people in a camera

events.subtitle: Free art installations at ADE Lab Village
events.categories: Audiovisual & Immersive Arts / Free A&C Events / Other / West
events.description:
After being cancelled during ADE 2025 due to the adverse weather conditions, Heliotrope by Heleen Blanken & Daniel de Bruin is back at the ADE Lab Village in Westerpark during the ADE week 2026.

Heliotrope is a kinetic installation inspired by the natural phenomenon in which plants orient their leaves and blossoms toward the sun. The work takes this principle as both a biological reference and a metaphor, exploring processes of energy reception, tropistic behaviour, the atomic movements inherent to living matter, and the pulsating rhythms embedded within the natural world. This idea is translated into a mirrored installation. The mechanically engineered installation moves its blades, diffusing light beams, and reflecting its surroundings in a chaotic and refracted image. events.title: Melting Image
events.subtitle: The longer you look, the more it changes.
events.categories: Exhibitions / Free A&C Events / Other / Centre
events.description:
Melting Image is a quiet resistance to how we consume images today — against the passive, one-dimensional scroll of the digital screen, it asks for presence instead of speed. Here, looking takes time, and the image only reveals itself to those willing to give it.An image is silkscreened onto layers of transparent material, then heat-formed until it lifts off the flat surface and takes on an organic, sculptural shape. Displayed in the gallery window, it turns the glass into a screen between street and space. Lit from behind by a slowly shifting projection, each layer catches the colour differently: parts of the image surface, others fade, never quite settling into one form. The longer you look, the more it keeps changing.Romina Koopman is a visual artist working at the edge of the tangible and the virtual, questioning how the digital image reshapes our perception of reality.

events.description:
In loving memory of Jelmar van Belle, who filmed these videos during the closing of De School and sadly passed away on 20 February 2026.In January 2024, the renowned Amsterdam nightclub De School closed its doors. For more than eight years, it offered the city a unique space where everyone could truly be themselves. Behind these doors, a world of expression, love, fashion, and identity emerged. Clubs like this are more than nightlife venues, they are breeding grounds for culture.

The culture that forms around Amsterdam’s underground nightlife is shaped by people who cannot easily be defined. They often remain invisible to the outside world, partly due to the strict no-picture policy. events.subtitle: An evocative deep-sea experience by Olafur Eliasson
events.categories: Exhibitions / Audiovisual & Immersive Arts / Ambient & Listening / Other / Centre / New Arts & Culture Venues / Deep Listening & Spatial Sound
events.description:
As you approach Deep Seeing Currents by Olafur Eliasson, you are slowly enveloped by darkness and the sounds of life underwater. Layers of oceanic cacophony – whale songs, rumbling of hydrothermal vents, and human-made noises, among others – surround you, while the vibrations can be felt throughout your entire body, emulating the experience of pressure in the deep sea. Above and around you, lights flash and seem to descend like the hypnotic circulation of marine snow, the organic and inorganic particles essential to life in the deep sea.The immersive sound of Deep seeing currents is brought to life by 4DSOUND. The exhibition is located inside the ARTIS Aquarium and can be visited with a valid ARTIS Park ticket. Tickets are available through the ARTIS website.

Pantheon Amsterdam brings together contemporary art, heritage and spirituality in a unique exhibition at Museum Ons’ Lieve Heer op Solder. Eight artists are creating new altarpieces and celebrations centred on stories of faith, identity, exclusion and recognition. Pantheon Amsterdam demonstrates that these subjects are not merely historical phenomena, but contemporary themes that continue to give meaning to the lives of many people.

By integrating and remixing classical music elements with live electronic composition influenced by ancestral rhythms, they reinterpret supposedly opposing liturgical ideologies. events.subtitle: A program on collecting Amsterdam's club and night culture
events.categories: Exhibitions / Free A&C Events / Other / West / Club Culture / New Arts & Culture Venues
events.description:
Presented as part of the Amsterdam Museum's 100th anniversary, with the support of ADE Arts & Culture and Podiumkunst.net

For decades, Amsterdam's club culture has been a breeding ground for art, music, and social movements. From the legendary venues of the 1980s to today's nightlife scene, these are stories that have shaped the city. Yet this heritage is largely absent from official archives and collections. How do we ensure that the history of Amsterdam's nightlife is preserved, and for whom?Two art installations by MRLYN and State OFFF form an archive for night and club culture in their own way. The exhibition explores what it means to collect club culture: which objects, stories, and experiences deserve a place in archives and collections? events.categories: Exhibitions / Beyond the Dancefloor / Other / New West / New Arts & Culture Venues
events.description: 99 years ago, Layla was filmed; the first Egyptian feature film. This marked the beginning of a film culture that became one of the shared languages ​​of the Arab world for decades.This exhibition, Dreams of Films – Films of Dreams, by Van Eesteren Museum and Moataz Rageb, brings back the visual world of cinema from that era. Here, you will discover original cinema posters, hand-painted billboards, and illustrated posters created by illustrators, calligraphers, and printers who are rarely known by name.In addition to images, sound and music also take center stage. Film music has always been inextricably linked to Egyptian cinema, and famous compositions were revived through another medium: on cassette tapes. AUDIO OBSCURA x JEFF MILLS PRESENT: JEFF MILLS' INTERPRETATION OF REMBRANDT'S 'DE NACHTWACHT'

Rembrandt’s De Nachtwacht became the starting point for a new artistic work by Jeff Mills, created and filmed inside the Rijksmuseum.Mills studied Rembrandt’s masterpiece and responded to it through his own art, bringing together electronic music, dance and visual art. events.description:
Rooted in Culture returns to ITA Amsterdam for it's fifth anniversary edition. This year's programme explores the journey of house music to Europe and the crucial role the UK played as its first European home. events.description: Forget the conference room. This is where ADE actually gets done. Since 2018, Exchange Asia has been quietly building the bridge nobody else bothered with, Asia's dance music scene and the West's, in the same space, trading more than just sets. This year, that bridge goes dark.BLACK MARKET takes the Boiler Room format and strips out everything that isn't essential: 10-12 artists, 45 minutes each, zero filler. But this isn't a line up to watch and forget. It's a market. Every DJ who steps up is here to trade : a sound, a contact, a booking, a favour, and the floor is built to make sure that trade actually happens. An Exchange Board on-site turns a room full of strangers into a five-minute conversation with exactly the right person.No cash fees for artists. No corporate sponsor logos plastered across the booth. events.subtitle: presented by Harmonic Dissonance
events.categories: Exhibitions / Audiovisual & Immersive Arts / Free A&C Events / Other / New West / New Arts & Culture Venues
events.description:
A monochromatic light instrument played through collective presence.

White Space is an immersive installation that transforms negative space into a place where strangers connect.At its heart, a monolith of intense blue and white light spins on its axis, casting compositions of monochromatic light and generative music that shift and dance among the audience. Responding to pose and position, the sculpture becomes an instrument, played by everyone present at once.Only by coordinating their positions and synchronising their poses can visitors reach the climax of the installation: illuminating the emptiness that separates them and transforming the negative space into White Space.White Space is an interactive light installation by artist Matthias Oostrik, who leads its concept, software, and production. events.subtitle: Free Public Exhibition
events.categories: Exhibitions / Free A&C Events / Funk / Baile Funk / East
events.description:
"Vira", in Portuguese, means to turn or transform something — a situation, a scenario — in a positive way. VIRA becomes the cultural link between Brazil and the Netherlands, pulsing with music, art, nightlife, and the vibrant energy of both countries.

During ADE Week, Studio/K will be transformed into a free public exhibition space where photography, film, and digital storytelling come together. A photography exhibition featuring images from São Paulo and Amsterdam highlights the connections between the two cities.

The program concludes with an indepth session on the 24th of October featuring members of Encosta and ONDA Collective, followed by "Beats & Bites," an informal networking event that brings together artists, musicians, creatives, visitors, and professionals from the Dutch and Brazilian creative sectors.

The exhibition is free to visit, Wed-Sat 16:00-22:00.

events.title: Welcome To The Club
events.subtitle: 30th Anniversary Party
events.categories: Nighttime events / Unique venues / Music Culture / Deep House / House / Tech-house / NDSM
events.description:
In 1996, DJ MAX launched a movement. 1300+ radio episodes, countless dancefloors from Ibiza to Croatia, and 30 years later, Welcome To The Club is returning to its Amsterdam home for the ultimate anniversary celebration.

We are taking over the iconic Van de Werf in Amsterdam-Noord for our third consecutive ADE showcase, and we’re bringing a global family of artists with us. Expect a masterclass in House music sub-genres, featuring a curated lineup of established pioneers and next-generation innovators from the USA, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands and beyond.

Originating in 1996 on National Public Radio (HRT - HR2) as one of Europe’s longest-running weekly electronic shows, the brand has broadcast over 1300 episodes and hosted events across the continent's clubbing capitals. For ADE 2026, the brand returns to its Amsterdam hub, Van de Werf, on Saturday, October 24th.

events.title: Ruby Emma Presents: ADE 30th Anniversary Showcase
events.subtitle: Four artists. Eight hours. One Saturday, start to finish.
events.categories: Nighttime events / Club nights / Intimate venues / Beyond the Dancefloor / House / Live / Techno / Bars
events.description:
Plenty of ADE nights start at midnight. This one starts at 18:00, in a hotel bar on a bend of the Amstel, and runs through to two.

Ruby Emma hosts the ADE 30th Anniversary Showcase on Saturday 24 October. Four artists, eight hours, one room.

FRITZ KALKBRENNER closes the night. The Berlin producer behind Sky and Sand takes over the decks for the final stretch.

Before him, MGUN, PHILIPP WOLF and TONIC WALTER (LIVE) build the room, moving from Afro House and driving grooves through melodic electronics to deep house and techno.

Eight hours gives you room to move. Come straight from a conference session, come on from somewhere else, or come at six and stay for all four. Nothing here asks you to build your Saturday around a single 90-minute window.

The bar's already open when you get here.

Tickets are on sale now – grab yours and join us for eight hours of music at Ruby Emma.

Live music

events.description:
Dokzaal collectives LOKAAL and Tell Me More team up with ADE for a showcase of local and international performers, spanning from experimental performance to dance floor goodness.

To start the evening, we've got a meal cooked by Amsterdam legend John Pastinaak in our community kitchen. Setting the tone for what's to come, Ines Barovac blesses us with a full-choir, avant-garde "dinner" performance, followed by sound mangler Ruben Kotkamp, cellist Lucija Gregov, and violinist Christine Cornwell for a blissful ambient serenade. As the night deepens, two dance floor magicians, Zoë Mc Pherson and XEPPO take over with live sets.

Tickets are sliding scale, and dinner tickets go quickly, so make sure you reserve in advance!

events.description:
Before they changed South Africa's electronic scene as GoldFish, Dominic Peters and David Pool were students by day, blowing the roof off many a house party by night. In recent years, the duo found international success with their dynamic sound of house, pop and jazz, filled with African rhythms, cheeky samples and endlessly upbeat hooks. On Saturday, October 24, the beloved duo returns to Amsterdam for a special ADE show in our Max.

These apparent opposites both long for connection, understanding and care. The vampire becomes a figure for the desire for those fleeting moments of pleasure and intimacy that remind us that we are alive, precisely in a world where certain bodies and lives risk becoming invisible.The eclipse is the starting point for the work. In colonial Mexico, the phenomenon was represented by Indigenous artists as the moment when the sun closes its eyes; the sun did not disappear, but rather we disappeared from its sight. From this perspective, Tlaseca asks to what extent our memories remain present, and whether we can return to them.Eclipse grew out of a series of letters that Tlaseca wrote from a deep longing for connection. events.title: 4AM KRU
events.categories: Nighttime events / Large venues / Bass & UK / Drum & Bass
events.description:
It would be easy to imagine 4am Kru were born in an instant flash of blinding light. After all, the truest way to experience their music is in the timeless white heat of a manic rave dancefloor, where they deliver their literally sweat-drenched live show. The way they distil the pure energy and spirit of early '90s rave and jungle feels so effortless that it seems driven by instinct alone.In reality, though, the story was anything but instant. Howie and Stu, the core of the Kru, spent years painstakingly experimenting and refining their sound before everything clicked into place and 4am Kru exploded into life. This ADE, they bring that raw energy to our stage!

events.title: Futures of Listening presents: Currents | Configuration III
events.subtitle: Spatial sound performances
events.categories: Live Performances / Electro & Wave / Alternative Electronic / Live / East / New Arts & Culture Venues / Recommended Arts & Culture Events / Deep Listening & Spatial Sound
events.description:
Futures of Listening comes to Amsterdam Dance Event 2026 with Currents, a four-day programme of experiments and performances in spatial sound at Loods6, from 22 to 25 October. Across three evenings of live and DJ sets, a day of workshops and demos, and a closing spatial sound meetup, artists work with changing sound system configurations to shape a different listening experience each night.

The programme takes place in the concrete Bagagehall of Loods6, a former passenger and freight terminal on the edge of the IJ. Speakers small and large are placed along the length of the hall, and sound moves between them across heights and distances. Currents is an experiment in what sound in space can mean: visitors can sit, lie down and walk through the space while performances take place at various points along the corridor.

events.description: As if she’s sitting next to you on the couch, Diamanda La Berge Dramm’s voice is intimate and immediate. Emerging from the serene Norwegian landscape, dublon is a major player in the recent jazz house explosion. His sounds blend intricate instrumentation with driving house rhythms, conjuring images of dimly-lit wine bars and long summer nights. Having collected over 200 millions streams, and with a European tour culminating in a Jazz Cafe headline show, dublon is now bringing his sounds into the very clubs he’s been so inspired by.

Nectar, his debut EP, is his most refined work yet, collating atmospheric toplines from vocalists and collaborations with renowned musicians Nathan Haines and Tour-Maubourg. It’s a collection of songs that emphasises his mastery of pop, classical and jazz sounds.

So far dublon has preformed as a DJ, but this fall he brings great jazz-musicians for a Live tour around Europe to show a different side of the project.

In this new documentary, we immerse ourselves in the mysterious world of one of the most iconic clubs in the world – and accompany very different people through their Berlin nights. We meet Tim, alias Raven Van Krueger, who wants to make it big as a drag artist. Elisa discovers a new sexuality with her friends, a BDSM couple loves publicly, a dog play duo lives stability and excess, David tries to fight his way out of addiction. And club founder Simon seems out of step with the times – like many who once laid the foundations of the legendary KitKatClub.

Performances, discussions about consent, tender conversations with fathers, encounters between bodies and souls. "KitKatClub: Kinks of Berlin" is a cinematic experience about freedom, intimacy, identity, sex, and unlearning shame—raw and poetic at the same time.

events.title: Thuishaven ADE Saturday Night: AFTERJAM
events.categories: Nighttime events / Intimate venues / House / Tech-house
events.description:
Thuishaven is not a club, or a warehouse. It’s a unique experience. Located on the Western outskirts of Amsterdam, the site is surrounded by heavy industry, massive oil tankers and scrap metal yards. Thuishaven has several stages, bars, surreal decoration pieces and curiosities. Incorporating materials purchased or found at neighboring scrap yards, the site radiates a raw and industrial atmosphere. During the winter set-up (October - April), all stages are housed indoor, in heated tents and a newly crafted hangar. The summer set-up (May - September) hosts a mesmerizing open air stage plus the option to use both tent and hangar for a raveyer vibe. With a track record of 200 festivals and counting, the site is ever evolving. Every new visit brings to light new details and new surprises—making it one of Amsterdam’s most extraordinary venues.

In 1992 the Warehouse, originally a peanut factory, located in the industrial West of Amsterdam hosted some of the very first large scale party raves called Multigroove. These nights set a milestone in Amsterdam's music development and party scene.Almost 20 years later, the mystical location re-opened its doors after being closed in 1993. Still with the same intention: to bring music from its purest side. events.description: Every person who walks into Charged becomes exactly that. A cloud of light gathers around you, pulled in by your presence, and moves when you move. Some people you meet in it carry the same charge as you, and so push each other's energy away. As magnetic poles repel, opposites attract.The work is about how we change each other's environment simply by being in it, positively or negatively, whether we mean to or not. Charging and discharging as a way of interacting between persons. The more people step in, the more chaotic it becomes. events.title: Melting Image
events.subtitle: The longer you look, the more it changes.
events.categories: Exhibitions / Free A&C Events / Other / Centre
events.description:
Melting Image is a quiet resistance to how we consume images today — against the passive, one-dimensional scroll of the digital screen, it asks for presence instead of speed. Here, looking takes time, and the image only reveals itself to those willing to give it.An image is silkscreened onto layers of transparent material, then heat-formed until it lifts off the flat surface and takes on an organic, sculptural shape. Displayed in the gallery window, it turns the glass into a screen between street and space. Lit from behind by a slowly shifting projection, each layer catches the colour differently: parts of the image surface, others fade, never quite settling into one form. The longer you look, the more it keeps changing.Romina Koopman is a visual artist working at the edge of the tangible and the virtual, questioning how the digital image reshapes our perception of reality.

Visitors can interact with the sleeping babies in real time by inputting sound through a microphone, connecting with them via the ChatGPT system. events.title: Selectors Sunday - Orbit Wax invites
events.subtitle: Percy (Orbit Wax) and resident selectors of a Sense of Place
events.categories: Music Culture / Beyond the Dancefloor
events.description:
Orbit Wax is an independent record shop for underground electronic music, and it lives inside a Sense of Place. Percy runs it. He picks the records, he prices them, and on Sundays he plays them.

On the last day of ADE he plays from the shelves, noon until six. What comes out of the crates: Japanese psychedelics from the 80s and 90s, dub techno, minimal, ambient, downtempo, 2000s tech house. The thread through all of it, in his words, is "an endless, dreamy, hypnotic sound". The day starts easy, builds through the afternoon and settles again towards six.

Through the day he invites our resident selectors to the decks with him: the people who play the room on other Sundays of the year.

Most of the records you hear are in the shop, a few metres from the turntable. Listen first, then take one home.

Free entry, no reservation. Seated. Coffee is served as on any Sunday.

A specialty coffee

events.subtitle: Audio Obscura x Jeff Mills
events.categories: Film & Documentaries / Free A&C Events / Other / South
events.description:
AUDIO OBSCURA x JEFF MILLS PRESENT: JEFF MILLS' INTERPRETATION OF REMBRANDT'S 'DE NACHTWACHT'

Rembrandt’s De Nachtwacht became the starting point for a new artistic work by Jeff Mills, created and filmed inside the Rijksmuseum.Mills studied Rembrandt’s masterpiece and responded to it through his own art, bringing together electronic music, dance and visual art. The resulting film has never been publicly shown.As part of ADE’s 30th anniversary, the film will be unveiled to the public for the very first time — returning to the very space in which it was conceived.From Thursday 22 to Sunday 25 October, the 50-minute film will be presented three times a day in the Rijksmuseum auditorium.Timeslots will be at 12PM, 2PM and 4PM.Admission is free and includes entry to the Rijksmuseum, courtesy of KPN as connectivity partner.Sign up before October 11, 23.59 to receive access by email to the tick

events.title: Thuishaven Sunday
events.subtitle: Polyamor presents: Davyboi invites
events.categories: Daytime events / Outdoor events / Hard Dance
events.description:
Thuishaven is not a club, or a warehouse. It’s a unique experience. Located on the Western outskirts of Amsterdam, the site is surrounded by heavy industry, massive oil tankers and scrap metal yards. Thuishaven has several stages, bars, surreal decoration pieces and curiosities. Incorporating materials purchased or found at neighboring scrap yards, the site radiates a raw and industrial atmosphere. During the winter set-up (October - April), all stages are housed indoor, in heated tents and a newly crafted hangar. The summer set-up (May - September) hosts a mesmerizing open air stage plus the option to use both tent and hangar for a raveyer vibe. With a track record of 200 festivals and counting, the site is ever evolving. Every new visit brings to light new details and new surprises—making it one of Amsterdam’s most extraordinary venues.

For ADE, we're taking over Skatecafé with a full day across two areas. A program built around artists we admire, rare back-to-backs and plenty of room for discovery. Skatecafe is a hybrid playground, part anarchic hangout and underground haven. What began as a warehouse in Amsterdam-Noord unravelled into a haven for wild ideas, unpredictable nights, and a community that thrives on DIY energy.Here, raves erupt in pitch-black bunkers, chaos spills onto the skate ramp and nothing ever follows a script. events.description:

events.title: Futures of Listening presents: Currents | Gathering Sounds: Spatial Sound Meetup
events.subtitle: by Futures of Listening
events.categories: Indepth / Free A&C Events / Ambient & Listening / Ambient / East / New Arts & Culture Venues / Deep Listening & Spatial Sound
events.description:
Gathering Sounds closes the Currents programme with a shift in register: from performance to practice, from audience to community. This is a day where the room turns inward, practitioners sharing what they're working on, and why.

Across an afternoon at Loods6, spatial sound practitioners take turns bringing something from their practice into the room: a tool, a patch, a speaker build, a piece in progress, a field recording, a research question, a score. Nothing here needs to be finished. This is a space for work that's still finding its shape, presented as an invitation to think and listen together.Gathering Sounds is part of a series of community events running throughout the Futures of Listening project, built to create space for exchange and connection outside of formal presentation contexts.Free entry.

Presented by FIBER Festival and 4DSOUND as part of Futures of Listening.

events.title: Aftershock: The Seismic Impact of Dubstep (2026)
events.subtitle: Book Launch - Presented by Sonic Boom
events.categories: Indepth / Dubstep / Centre
events.description:
Lauren Martin, the Scottish, London-based music writer and editor (formerly of RBMA, DJ Mag, and others), published "Aftershock: The Seismic Impact of Dubstep" in 2026 through Velocity Press. The first book on dubstep history, it's an oral history of the British electronic music genre’s origin story, as told through extensive interviews with 28 key artists and industry figures, and exclusive photography and visual ephemera from artists and photographers. In this hosted Q&A session featuring exclusive photography and video footage, Martin will discuss dubstep history and influence, how its sound and principles show up in contemporary music scenes, and the importance of archiving music culture.

EarthSonic, ARTIS and ADE Arts & Culture, with the support of the European Space Agency, present:

What if we could not only see how our planet is changing, but hear it?For more than fifty years, satellites have been observing Earth, generating an extraordinary archive of data about our changing planet. In 1992 the Warehouse, originally a peanut factory, located in the industrial West of Amsterdam hosted some of the very first large scale party raves called Multigroove. Still with the same intention: to bring music from its purest side. And dance until sunrise.Today the Warehouse is home to some of the city's most renowned party concepts such as Hyte, Welcome to the Future indoor festival, Reaktor and Luciano & friends.
